title: adaptive qk-kv fusion with prefetching and rotary interleave for long-context throughput
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Long-context workloads (>=16k tokens) dominate several customer workloads. Existing FlashAttention and separate QK/KV kernels yield suboptimal memory traffic when serving long sequences with continuous batching and active KV caching. This PR introduces an adaptive kernel strategy that fuses QK compute and KV accumulation paths where beneficial, plus a lightweight KV prefetcher and a rotary-interleave layout to reduce memory bandwidth and kernel launch overhead. Design: 1) New fused kernels (CUDA) that compute QK scores and simultaneously write/aggregate KV fragments for future decode steps. These kernels are selected when sequence-length, batch composition, and kv cache hit heuristics indicate net win. 2) Adaptive kernel dispatcher: runtime heuristics (histogram of seq lengths, batch fill factor, GPU occupancy) choose between FlashAttention variants, fused QK-KV path, or the legacy split kernels. 3) KV prefetcher: background thread schedules small prefetches of cache pages for the most likely next-tokens based on route-level bandit policy, reducing tail latency on cache-miss heavy workloads. 4) Rotary interleave: reorganizes rotary embeddings in-memory to make fused kernels use contiguous loads for q/k/v, reducing strided accesses on long context. Implementation notes: - CUDA kernels implemented in runtime/attention with careful register/block tuning for Ampere/Blackwell GPUs. - Dispatcher lives in runtime/attention/kernel_dispatcher.cc and exposes a policy hook for testing via env vars. - Continuous batcher updated to expose batch shape histograms and to annotate requests with expected next-token probabilities (used by prefetcher). - Small pinned-memory prefetch buffer added to runtime/kv_cache, with heuristics to avoid polluting hot-cache entries. Tests & validation: microbenchmarks (tests/benchmarks/attn_long_context.py) show median throughput gain of 18% on 32k-context benchmarks vs previous flash-attn-only baseline, p50 decode latency reduced 12% for batched streaming, and token-cost reduction of ~9% under production-like mixes due to fewer kernel launches and lower GPU memory traffic. We ran full GPU integration tests, perf canary, and private deployment smoke tests. Rollout plan: feature gated behind env REDWOOD_FEATURE_ADAPTIVE_FUSE and opt-in in Dedicated as default off for first 2 weeks. Safety: we added deterministic fallbacks and correctness unit tests comparing fused outputs to reference split-kernel outputs for a variety of dtype/seq-length/model-size combinations. Backwards compatibility: no API changes. See release_notes for user-visible improvements.

discussion: Ethan Park: Can we get deterministic unit tests that cover rotary offsets and half-precision edge cases? Maya Chen: Added tests in tests/unit/test_fused_vs_split.py that compare fp16/fp32 outputs and several rotary offset patterns across seq lengths up to 32k. Also added a CI perf gate that runs a reduced microbenchmark on each PR. Sofia Ruiz: Concerned about polluting the KV cache with speculative prefetches for low-probability tokens. How do we avoid regressions for small batch sizes? Maya Chen: Prefetcher uses a conservative bandit with decay and an LRU guard; for small batches (<4) prefetching is disabled. We also added telemetry to monitor prefetch hit/miss ratios and an env flag REDWOOD_PREFETCH_ENABLE to turn this off. Liam O'Connor: Any impact on memory footprint for multi-tenant Dedicated? Maya Chen: Pinned buffer defaults to 32MB per GPU and is configurable by deployment; we added a guard to cap total pinned usage to 1% of GPU memory by default. QA: Found a race in the dispatcher when batch histogram updates happen concurrently — fixed in commit f90c2e1 and added a mutex around histogram writes. Post-merge: ops will run a canary for two days on a small fleet before enabling the feature by default for internal staging.
release_notes: Improves long-context inference throughput and latency by introducing an adaptive fused QK-KV kernel path, KV prefetching, and memory-layout optimizations for rotary embeddings. Gains: ~18% throughput on 32k-context benchmarks, ~12% p50 decode latency reduction, ~9% token-cost reduction in mixed workloads. Feature is behind REDWOOD_FEATURE_ADAPTIVE_FUSE and off by default for Dedicated; safe rollout planned.
